sentences.text:
Deeravath Kishan, Hyderabad And 3 ... vs P Sadanand,
Secunderabad And Anr on 21 July, 2023
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice Namavarapu Rajeshwar Rao
 M.A.C.M.A.No.2732 Of 2015
Judgment:

This MACMA is filed by the appellants/petitioners under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act,
aggrieved by the order and decree dated 30.06.2014, passed in M.V.O.P.No.1263 of 2011 on the file of the Chairman, Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal- cum-XIV Additional Chief Judge (FTC), City Civil Courts, Hyderabad) (for short "the Tribunal").
2.

entities.text: Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal- cum-XIV Additional Chief Judge (FTC), City Civil Courts, Hyderabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: For the sake of convenience, the parties will be hereinafter referred to as they are arrayed before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are that the petitioners filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, claiming compensation of Rs.3,00,000/- on account of the death of Smt. Deeravath Bhuli @ Bhuli Bai (hereinafter referred to as "deceased") stated that on 23.03.2011 the deceased along with her relative Sri Rajan was proceeding on a motorcycle from ECIL X roads in order to go to 2 RRN,J Chakripuram.

On the way at about 23.15 hours when they reached near Kushaiguda Bus Stop, one DCM Van bearing No.AP-10-W-1885 (Old registration No.MH-43E-1458) came in the opposite direction and it was driven by its driver at a high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed the motorcycle of the deceased.
As a result, the deceased fell down and had sustained grievous injuries and died on the spot.
The police of Kushaiguda Police Station had registered a case in Cr.No.194 of 2011 under Section 304-A IPC.
It is further stated that the deceased was aged 50 years and earning Rs.4,000/- per month as a labourer and used to contribute the same for the maintenance of the petitioners.
Hence, the claim petition.

4. Before the Tribunal, respondent No.1 remained ex parte and respondent No.2 filed counter denying the petition allegations and contended that the claim petition is liable to be dismissed for non-joinder of necessary parties and there was contributory negligence.

4.1 In the additional counter it is stated that as per the petition and chief affidavit of petitioners on 3 RRN,J 23.03.2011 at about 23.15 hours while the deceased G. Rajan was proceeding as a rider along with two pillion riders i.e. his wife Jannu Bai and mother-in-law Buli Bai on the motorcycle bearing No.AP-29K-1917 in order to go to ECIL from Chakrapuram and when they reached Kushaiguda Bus stop at that time the crime vehicle i.e. DCM Van bearing No.AP-10W-188 came in a rash and negligent manner at high speed and dashed the motorcycle.
Police filed a chargesheet under Section 304-A IPC and under Section 181 of the M.V. Act against the driver of said Van.
The crime vehicle was driven by a person who had no driving license at the time of the accident and it violates policy conditions and respondent No.2 is not liable to pay any compensation.

entities.text: Deeravath Kishan, Hyderabad And 3 ... vs P Sadanand, Secunderabad And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 1 5. To prove their case, petitioners examined PW.1 and got marked Exs.A1 to A5 were marked.
On behalf of respondent No.2 RW.1 was examined and Ex.B1 to B3 were marked.

6. On appreciation of the evidence on record, the Tribunal allowed the O.P. in part by awarding compensation of Rs.7,33,400/- with interest @ 7.5% p.a. from the date of 4 RRN,J petition till the date of realization.
Challenging the same, the present appeal is filed by the petitioners praying to enhance the compensation amount.

7. Learned counsel appearing for the petitioners inter-alia contended that the Tribunal erred in considering the monthly income of the deceased on the lower side and failed to award compensation under the conventional heads as per the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi1.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly, prayed to allow the appeal.
8. Per contra, learned counsel appearing for respondent No.2 contended that the Tribunal was justified in passing the impugned order, which calls for no interference by this Court.

Accordingly,
prayed to dismiss the appeal.
9. Heard both sides.
Perused the record.

10. The first issue with regard to the manner of the accident and liability imposed upon the respondents was decided against the respondents and as the same is not challenged, it has attained finality.

The only issue which (2017) 16 SCC 680.
5 RRN,J needs to be considered is with regard to the quantum of compensation.

11. It is noticed from the impugned order that the Tribunal assessed the monthly income of the deceased at Rs.4,000/-, whereas, the learned Counsel for the petitioners contended that the income of the deceased should have been taken on the higher side i.e. at Rs.6,000/- p.m.
In support of his claim, the learned Counsel for the petitioners has relied upon the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court reported in Laxmidhar Nayak and ors.

Vs. Jugal Kishore Behera and ors.2 wherein, it was held the High Court as well as Tribunal did not keep in view the contribution of the deceased in the household work, being a labourer and also maintaining her husband, her daily income should be fixed at Rs.150/- per day and Rs.4,500/- per month.

He has further relied upon another decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court reported in Rajendra Singh and ors. Vs. National Insurance Company Limited and ors.3 wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court considered the notional income of the deceased housewife at Rs.5,000 p.m. (2018) 1 SCC 746.

entities.text: Rajendra Singh and ors. Vs. National Insurance Company Limited and ors.3
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There is no ambiguity with regard to the avocation of the deceased and as such, applying the above decisions to the present case, the income of the deceased is taken at Rs.5,000/-

p.m. An addition of 25% on the monthly income is to be effected in view of the decision rendered in Pranay Deeravath Kishan, Hyderabad And 3 ... vs P Sadanand, Secunderabad And Anr on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115370793/
2 Sethi (supra).

entities.text: Pranay Deeravath Kishan, Hyderabad And 3 ... vs P Sadanand, Secunderabad And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Thus, the annual income of the deceased would come to Rs.75,000/- (Rs.5,000/- +
25% x 12).
As the dependants are 4 in number, 1/4th deduction is to be made from the annual income of the deceased.
The appropriate multiplier as per the decision of Sarla Verma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation4 is "13".

entities.text: Sarla Verma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation4
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Thus, the total loss of dependency would come to Rs.7,31,250/-
(Rs.75,000 - 1/4th x 13).

13. The Tribunal awarded Rs.25,000/- towards funeral expenses and Rs.1,00,000/- towards loss of love and affection and the same needs to be altered and compensation under different eligible heads as per settled law has to be awarded.

The petitioners are entitled to compensation under conventional heads as per the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Pranay Sethi (supra) and Magma Insurance (2009) 6 SCC 121.
7 RRN,J Company Ltd. Vs. Nanu Ram @ Chuhru Ram5.

entities.text: RRN,J Company Ltd. Vs. Nanu Ram @ Chuhru Ram5
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The petitioners are awarded Rs.15,000/-
towards loss of estate and Rs.15,000/- towards funeral expenses and an additional 10% on these amounts, totalling to Rs.33,000/-.
The 4th petitioner is entitled to Rs.40,000/- towards loss of parental consortium as she was a minor at the time of the death of the deceased.

In all, the petitioners are entitled to Rs.8,04,250/- (Rs.7,31,250 + Rs.33,000 + Rs.40,000)
14.

In the result, the M.A.C.M.A is allowed in part and the compensation amount awarded by the Tribunal is enhanced from Rs.7,33,400/- to Rs.8,04,250/- (Rupees Eight Lakh Four Thousand and Two hundred Fifty only) with interest @7.5 % p.a. from the date of petition till the date of realization.

The respondents are directed to deposit the said amount with costs and interest after deducting the amount, if any, already deposited, within two months from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment.

On such deposit, the petitioners are permitted to withdraw the same in accordance with the manner and proportion as determined by the Tribunal, subject to payment of deficit Court fee, within two 52018 Law Suit (SC) 904 8 RRN,J months from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment.

It is needless to say that the Tribunal already observed that respondent No.2 is entitled to recover the amount paid by it from respondent No.1 as per the law, the same is being reiterated by this Court.
There shall
be no order as to costs.
As a sequel of which, miscellaneous petitions, if any pending, shall stand closed.
NAMAVARAPU RAJESHWAR RAO, J 21st July, 2023 BDR/PRV Deeravath Kishan, Hyderabad And 3 ... vs P Sadanand, Secunderabad And Anr on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115370793/
